_comment: Enumerated, FIXED tajweed rules in the Hafs 'an 'Asim reading that no shipped dataset (tajweed.json / tajweed_cpfair.json) marks (issue #291). These are citable facts of the reading, not derived heuristics, so they are recorded here for a future reviewed implementation. NOTE: this file is a documented REFERENCE — it is NOT yet wired into generate_database.py. Per #291 the derived recitation rules require scholarly review against a printed tajweed mushaf before shipping.

sakt._comment: السكت — a brief pause without breath. The source text marks these with U+06DC (ARABIC SMALL HIGH SEEN). Reconciliation of the 7 U+06DC occurrences in text_arabic (the audit asked where the 'extra 3' came from):

obligatory_hafs_sakt.reason: sakt on the alif of عِوَجَا before قَيِّمًا
sakt on the alif of مَرْقَدِنَا
sakt on the noon of مَنْ (prevents idgham into رَاقٍ)
sakt on the lam of بَلْ (prevents idgham into رَانَ)

additional_sakt.reason: sakt on the ه of مَالِيَهْ before هَلَكَ — prevents idgham of the two hā's. Commonly listed as the 5th Hafs sakt; the '4 places' count omits it.

not_sakt_same_sign.reason: U+06DC here is the small seen written OVER the ṣād — an alternate-reading marker (yabsuṭu read with ص in Hafs, the س noted), NOT a sakt.
same small-seen-over-ṣād alternate-reading marker, not a sakt.

special_pronunciations.reason: the rā is pronounced with imālah (tilting toward kasra/yā); marked in the text with U+06EA on the rā.
ishmām — lip-rounding on the (assimilated) noon; marked with U+06EB.
tasheel — the second hamza is 'eased' between hamza and alif; marked with U+06EC.
naql — the hamza's vowel is transferred onto the preceding lām (al-ism → alism).

istila_letters._comment: Isti'lā (elevated) letters are always pronounced heavy (tafkhīm): خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ. Deterministic — no context needed.

waqf_signs._comment: Stop signs present in text_arabic but currently unstyled (occurrence counts verified against text_arabic).

signs.name: three dots — embracing stop (mu'ānaqah): stop at one of the pair, not both
sīn — sakt (see the sakt table above)
